Zoo Toss Rules

Roll the animal dice and fill your own card with the animals it shows. Every animal on a full card is one point. Whoever has the most points at the end wins.

The rules

The goal
Every card shows three to five animals, and every animal is worth one point: a full card with five animals brings five points. The game has 30 cards.
Your own card
At the start everyone gets a card from the pile. It is your own card: nobody else rolls for it. Two more cards lie open.
Your turn
On your turn you roll once, with as many dice as your card still needs. Every die that shows an animal of your card goes onto the card and stays there, marked with a tick. Then it is the next player's turn. On your next turn you roll again for the animals that are still missing.
The paw
The sixth side of the dice shows a paw. It is a joker: you put it on the card yourself. Tap a free place of an animal the card still needs. If only one animal is missing, or there are as many paws as free places, the paws go on by themselves.
A new card
When your card is full, you get its points. On your next turn you tap one of the two open cards and roll for it at once. A big card brings more points but needs more turns. A card with many different animals fills more easily than one that needs the same animal two or three times.
The end
When someone reaches 12 points, the round is played to its end, so that everyone has rolled equally often. Then whoever has the most points wins; with equal points the win is shared. With two to four players a game takes about five minutes. After the computers' turns you see their cards and dice and tap Next. There is no time limit, and nothing has to be read: every card and every die shows pictures.

Example

Your card shows three lions and a monkey. You roll four dice: lion, penguin, paw, giraffe. The lion goes onto the card. For the paw you tap a free place, for example the monkey. Two places for lions are still open: on your next turn you roll two dice.
